If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over last 5 days, reduce forecast by 2–4% in early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) over last 5 days, increase forecast by 2–4% in early horizon (1–7 days) to offset pessimism.  
In mid horizon (8–15 days), if sentiment swings from positive to negative, reduce forecast by 3–5% for the next 3 days to reflect sentiment reversal.  
In late horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment remains negative and forecast is still above 70, reduce by 5–7% to align with downward trend.  
If sentiment is mixed (alternating 0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 1–3% in late horizon to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is mixed and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast by 1–3% in late horizon to counteract sentiment-induced underestimation.
